title: Morning Bid: Feeding the AI beast
source_used: Reuters Morning Bid (text read on Livemint)
key_facts: Reuters's Morning Bid column by Ankur Banerjee says investor angst over AI bellwethers' appetite for capital has cast a shadow over markets.
OpenAI told investors its September annualised revenue was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signalled earlier, Reuters reported.
Australian data centre operator Firmus shelved its $5 billion IPO and chose a private fundraising round instead.
SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle are expected to raise billions of dollars to buy high-end AI chips.
Morgan Stanley estimates AI infrastructure will need $1.5 trillion in external financing by 2028, as interest rates rise to combat inflation from higher energy prices.
Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel and a months-long global bond selloff has pushed borrowing costs to multi-decade highs, most painfully in France.
quote_evidence: Investor angst over AI bellwethers' seemingly insatiable appetite for capital to build the infrastructure necessary for the technology to start paying off has cast a shadow over markets
why_it_matters_hint: The cost of paying for AI is rising just as the proof it pays off is being questioned.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); text read on Livemint (Reuters feed). It is a market commentary column, so some lines are the author's reading of the mood.
